title: Love for Whom?
arabic: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يُبَشِّرُ ٱللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ ۗ قُل لَّآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا إِلَّا ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ
translation: “That is the good news God gives His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say: I ask of you no reward for this except love for the near of kin.”

shia.label: Shia emphasis
shia.body: 'The near of kin' are the Prophet's own family - ʿAlī, Fāṭima, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn. He commands every believer to love them; that love is his mission's whole reward.

sunni.label: Sunni emphasis
sunni.body: 'The near of kin' is the Prophet's blood tie to the Quraysh. He asks his own tribe for no reward - only to honour the kinship they share with him.

voiceover.hook: The Prophet asked for just one reward - love. But love for whom? Two great traditions answer that differently.
voiceover.payoff: Three words - 'love for the near of kin.' One tradition hears a command to love the Prophet's family. The other, a plea to his own tribe: honour the kinship between us.
voiceover.question: Which of these two readings resonates with you
